column1: # Mega Twins / Chiki Chiki Boys (CPS1 `mtwins`) ARRANGE trigger map
#   -> Chiki Chiki Boys (Japan), PC Engine CD-ROM2 CD-DA.
# STATUS: COMPLETE. Every row below is USER EAR-CONFIRMED. Nothing is guessed.
# Arcade cues with no CD counterpart are listed explicitly and fail open to the
# arcade original, which is the correct outcome for them.
# === DISTINCTNESS: SETTLED, INCLUDED ===
# User verdict: "PCE is definitely arranged and deserves inclusion." The PCE CD-DA
# is a genuine re-arrangement, NOT a recording of arcade audio -- 25 isolated
# arcade renders x 24 CD tracks scored p50 0.012..0.044 against a known-render
# band of 0.65-0.94 and a CTRL- floor of ~0.04. See internal research notes
# === LOOPING: NO CROSSFADE REQUIRED ===
# Every recovered cue calls CD_PLAY ($E012) with play mode 1 = "Infinite repeat
# play": the DRIVE repeats the whole track with no further command from the game.
# No cue names an address inside a track, so there is NO authored inner loop point
# anywhere in this game. Whole-track repeat, same as Sega CD MSCPLAYR on `ffight`.
# === HOW THE MAPPING WAS ESTABLISHED ===
# Machine methods FAILED to settle this and must not be cited as support:
#   * waveform NCC (xcorr_id.py) only proves "not the same recording" -- it cannot
#     tell a re-performed cover from unrelated music, and every pair sat at the floor.
#   * chroma (chroma_id.py) DOES NOT survive a change of sound hardware: on an
#     ear-confirmed `ffight` CPS1-vs-SegaCD control it rated a KNOWN-IDENTICAL
#     composition at +0.069, the noise floor, and mis-paired 3 of 4. See its header.
#   * PCE-duration / arcade-loop-period ratio is NOT a usable filter. Confirmed
#     pairs span 1.11x .. 7.49x; a 0.9-5.0 band excluded 2 correct pairs (cmd18->tr21
#     at 7.49x, cmd1f->tr22 at 6.83x) and never once caught a wrong alignment.
# The map is ORDINAL WITH SKIPS, and every skip was found BY EAR, not predicted.
# === ARCADE BGM ENUMERATION (corrected) ===
# 27 BGM total. An initial sweep found 25 by requiring audio to still be sounding at
# the end of a 45 s render -- a rule that structurally excludes anything that ENDS,
# so it silently dropped both fanfares (cmd16, cmd1c). Commands 0x41-0xff were also
# swept (191 cmds): all sound effects / OKI PCM, no BGM. cmd8c aliases cmd16 and
# cmd92 aliases cmd1c (p50 0.985 / 0.973); cmd5d==cmdd3, cmd6b~=cmde1.
# NOTE for strider/forgottn: the same "sustained to end" rule would drop THEIR
# fanfares and stage-clear jingles too. Use the corrected classifier from the start.
# === CD SIDE ===
# 26 CD tracks: tr02 and tr26 are MODE1/2352 data; tr01 is the spoken Japanese
# "this is not a regular CD" CD-ROM2 warning. 23 music tracks, tr03..tr25.
# tr03 is PCE-EXCLUSIVE -- no arcade counterpart exists. It is also the only cue
# addressed by INDEX 01 (+2.000 s pregap skip) rather than a plain track boundary.
# tr24 is played by NO recovered cue (it appears only as an END boundary in the
# tr23 entry) yet is plainly arcade cmd15's arrangement -- so the statically
# recovered cue table has at least one gap. Harmless here: this pack maps arcade
# commands directly to CD audio and never consults the PCE cue table at runtime.
# === CODE ANALYSIS: WHY THE COUNTS DIFFER (27 arcade BGM vs 23 CD tracks) ===
# ARCADE DISPATCH (68K program image, che_30/35 + che_31/36 interleaved).
# Music is a 128-byte RING QUEUE of {fade, command} pairs in work RAM at
# a5+$8E3A, index at a5+$8E39, drained one entry per frame at prog 0x0005F0:
#     LEA ($8E3A,A5),A0 / MOVE.B ($8E39,A5),D0 / CMPI.W #$FFFF,(0,A0,D0)
#     MOVE.B (0,A0,D0),$800189   ; fade byte
#     MOVE.B (1,A0,D0),$800181   ; command byte
#     MOVE.W #$FFFF,(0,A0) / ADDQ.B #2,D0 / ANDI.B #$7F,D0
# The fade byte is pushed SEPARATELY from the command byte, which is why the
# CPS+ trigger format's independent fade/verb split matches this game natively.
# Idle/stop is MOVE.W #$00FF,$800180 at prog 0x0005E6 -- confirms idle byte 0xff.
# PCE DISPATCH. Cue index lives at $D821; the selector at CPU $D9F5 does
#     LDA $D821 / STZ $01 / (ASL A, ROL $01) x3 / ADC #$22 / ADC #$DE
# i.e. entry = $DE22 + index*8, then JSR $D806. 27 STA $D821 sites exist.
# Cues 2-14 and 17 are NEVER selected by an immediate -- only via TXA (stage
# index), so they are the stage BGM. Cues 0,1,15,16,18,19,20,21 are selected by
# explicit LDA #n at event sites; cue1 (tr03) has 4 sites / 2 distinct code
# paths (the other 2 are overlay copies), so tr03 is genuinely played.
# *** tr24 IS ORPHANED CONTENT ON THE PCE DISC ***
# The 22 cues reference tr03..tr23 and tr25. tr24 is referenced by NO cue -- it
# occurs only as the END boundary of the tr23 entry. Yet tr24 is plainly a
# finished arrangement of arcade cmd15 (ear-confirmed). Capcom arranged, mastered
# and pressed it, then never wired it to a cue. THIS PACK PLAYS IT (row 0x15),
# restoring a track the PC Engine release never plays.
# Complementary case: tr03 is played by the PCE game but has no arcade cue, so it
# has no row here and is not used by this pack.
# THE 5 DROPPED ARCADE CUES are 3 fanfares (0x13, 0x16, 0x1c) and 2 boss themes
# (0x1b, 0x1e) -- short cues the port left on the PC Engine's internal sound chip
# instead of spending CD-DA tracks on them ("some used the PC Engine's sound
# chip"). They fail open to the arcade original, which is correct for them.
# cmd        arcade sound-command byte (68K latch 0x800180)
# verb       play = VERB_PLAY(1); none = VERB_NONE(0)
# suppress   1 = substitute idle byte so the Z80 never starts the native music
# track      CD-DA track supplying the arrangement; "-" = none, fail open to arcade
# label      what the cue is
# evidence   how the row was established
cmd

# --- FANFARES -> FAIL OPEN to arcade FM (user decision, on measured evidence) ---
# These are NOT mapped to tr03 (a tempting purpose-match).  Reasons:
#   * MELODY: user ear-checked -- cmd16/cmd1c do not sound like tr03.
#   * LOOP BEHAVIOUR (measured from deterministic arcade renders, 1s resolution):
#       cmd16  ~8s then silence   -> ONE-SHOT fanfare
#       cmd1c  ~11s then silence  -> ONE-SHOT fanfare
#       cmd5e  ~15s then silence  -> ONE-SHOT fanfare
#       cmd13  181s of 191s active -> CONTINUOUS looping BGM, NOT a fanfare at all
#     tr03 is a single 69 s track; it cannot be both a one-shot (for 16/1c/5e) and
#     a loop (for 13), and it matches none of them melodically. Forcing it created
#     a wrong pairing in all four cases.
# cmd16/cmd1c/cmd5e ARE one code-level cue: the arcade picks a stage-variant at
# prog 0x1E5E6 / 0x1E630 (CMPI.B #$03/#$09,($8F64,A5)). cmd13 is separate.
# All four now fail open (verb=none, suppress=0 -> unwritten -> arcade FM plays),
# same mechanism as the secret cues below. tr03 is left PCE-only/unused.
